articles.title: After England setback, Babar Azam set for first domestic first-class game in seven years
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan captain Babar Azam is set to return to domestic first-class cricket for the first time in nearly seven years, with the Pakistan Cricket Board.
articles.body: Pakistan captain Babar Azam is set to return to domestic first-class cricket for the first time in nearly seven years, with the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) keen to see him back in action following Pakistan’s disappointing Test tour of England.Babar to represent Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) against Kingsmen Academy in the ongoing President’s Trophy Grade-I competition, starting September 18. His return comes after Pakistan suffered a 0-3 series whitewash in England and the PCB made sweeping changes to the touring squad and coaching staff.PCB wants Babar back in red-ball cricketBabar has not played domestic first-class cricket since 2019, when he represented Central Punjab in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy. OGDCL sports head Farah Batool said the PCB had sent his name to the team for inclusion as a guest player.“Babar’s kit has been ordered and he will decide whether to play in the match from September 18 or from September 24 in the third-round game,” Batool said.Shaheen, Haris among centrally contracted players in actionBabar is not the only centrally contracted Pakistan player featuring in domestic red-ball cricket after the England tour. Fast bowlers Shaheen Shah Afridi and Haris Rauf have also turned out for their respective teams in the President’s Trophy.Shaheen has represented KRL, claiming four wickets in an innings, while Haris picked up a five-wicket haul for PTV. Haris, who has played only one Test, against England in 2022, when he suffered an injury after bowling 13 overs, has expressed his willingness to return to Pakistan’s Test setup.“If I can be useful for Pakistan because of my pace, I would gladly play Test cricket,” he said.The fast bowler, who is primarily known for his T20 performances, had declined to play the Test series in Australia in December 2023, citing the need to manage his workload. His central contract was also suspended for a period before being restored.Babar’s captaincy under scrutiny after England whitewashBabar was reappointed Pakistan’s Test captain in July and has since overseen a 1-1 series draw against the West Indies and a 0-3 defeat to England. The PCB’s decision to make seven changes to the squad and remove head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul after the second Test at Lord’s reportedly came without consulting or informing Babar.Pakistan’s defeat in the second Test came inside three days, prompting major changes ahead of the final match of the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Leicestershire deducted 27 points and on brink of relegation from County Championship Division One
articles.summary: Leicestershire are on the brink of relegation from County Championship Division One after being deducted 27 points for breaching pitch regulations.
articles.body:
Leicestershire are on the brink of relegation from Division One of the County Championship after being deducted 27 points for breaching pitch regulations in their victory over Glamorgan in August.

The points penalty imposed by the independent Cricket Discipline Panel (CDP) midway through their penultimate match of the season meant the Foxes have dropped to the bottom of the table.

In his interview with the Cricket Regulator before the tribunal hearing, Leicestershire's head groundsman Callum Lewin said there were "circumstances leading up to the game that were just out of my control".

They included an "unscheduled Bollywood filming event" taking place at Uptonsteel Grace Road four days before the start of the match, while Lewin also referenced the exceptionally hot weather in the build-up as another possible reason for the pitch being dry.

The pitch was rated as "poor" in the match referee's report.

Leicestershire's punishment consists of the loss of all 19 points earned in the win over Glamorgan, an extra eight-point penalty and a £5,000 fine. A further eight-point deduction has been suspended for a year.

They can appeal the sanction within 10 working days.

In a statement, , external the club said it "notes the Cricket Discipline Panel's decision" and was "reviewing its position and considering all available options".

If the Foxes fail to beat Hampshire in their ongoing home game, their return to Division Two will be confirmed.

But they face a tough task to do so after Hampshire closed day two on 255-3 in their second innings - a lead of 225.

Just above the relegation places, the survival chances of both Glamorgan and Essex have been increased by Leicestershire's loss of points.

The Foxes' battle to avoid the drop in their first season back in Division One after a 22-year exile had been boosted by the 42-run win over Glamorgan three weeks earlier.

Before that, they had won just one match on their top-flight return after winning promotion as Division Two title winners last season.

When Leicestershire beat Glamorgan on 23 August it was immediately clear they would be in for an anxious wait to discover if the way the pitch played would have consequences.

The match officials, led by referee Ian Ramage, asked for the ECB's pitch and grounds advisor Andy Mackay to carry out an inspection after the game concluded.

After the match, Glamorgan head coach Richard Dawson said conditions were "tough" for batters.

Leicestershire head coach Alfonso Thomas added the surface had been prepared in the same way as the pitch used against Yorkshire - a game the Foxes won by an innings and 39 runs in June - although he acknowledged it was "a bit drier than what we wanted" for the match against Glamorgan.

The starting point for punishment for a pitch rated as "poor" is a 16-point deduction and this was reduced to eight points at the tribunal because of several mitigating factors.

Among them were Leicestershire's "early admission that the pitch was substandard" and this being the "first rating of below average, poor or unfit" in the previous 24 months.

A section of the judgement read: "The tribunal also takes into account Leicestershire's full co-operation with the Cricket Regulator's investigation, the fact that there was no intention to deliberately create a pitch with uneven bounce and the extreme weather conditions which do amount to some mitigation. This was not a case of cheating."

Analysis: Foxes 'gutted' about points deduction

I doubt I am being controversial by saying the pitch against Glamorgan did not play as expected. There was uneven bounce from early in the match and players were regularly getting hit on the hands.

They went for a "mullet" - shorter grass at the ends of the pitch and longer in the middle - which they have tried this week against Hampshire, to little effect, and the match before the game in question, against Yorkshire, and there was no extreme movement or bounce.

The same could not be said for this wicket.

Leicestershire felt we had a good game, which went for four days and included two scores of 90 or more. With low scores around the country that week, they did not think this pitch warranted further punishment.

The Foxes are gutted about this. They had worked so hard to work themselves back into a survival battle, only for this to ruin their chances of staying up after a 23-year wait. They need to beat Hampshire now, then title-chasing Warwickshire, and hope results elsewhere go their way. That is unlikely.

They would argue a 27-point deduction is severe and would also question whether pitches that lead to high-scoring bore draws deserve similar treatment, as well as other low-scoring pitches. However, the fact remains the club knew the rules before deciding on this pitch and it has cost them.

articles.title: County Championship: Warwickshire seal two-day win over Essex to boost title hopes as Sam Hain stars
articles.summary: Wednesday's County Championship cricket sees Warwickshire boost title hopes with two-day win vs Essex; Somerset still in title mix; Watch England's second T20 vs Sri Lanka live on Sky Sports Cricket and Sky Sports Main Event from 6pm on Thursday (6.30pm first ball)
articles.body:
Sam Hain's unbeaten 88 helped the Bears to a first-innings lead of 57 and then Manav Suthar's five for 75 saw Essex bowled out for 189 in their second innings.

Zen Malik's 51 and an unbeaten 22 from Hain saw the visitors ease to their target of 133 for the loss of two wickets.

Somerset also remain in the hunt for the title after putting themselves in a strong position against Yorkshire .

Talismanic all-rounder Craig Overton top-scored with 64 off 111 balls as Division One leaders Somerset recovered from 86 for eight to 201 all out in reply to Yorkshire's first-innings 212 all out.

After falling as one of eight wickets for Yorkshire's excellent new-ball quick Ben Cliff, he then struck twice with the new ball himself as the hosts advanced their second innings to 128 for six and a lead of 139.

Sussex have the advantage at Hove as they ended the day on 308 for six in reply to Nottinghamshire's 240.

Tom Clarke hit 89 and Charlie Tear (50) and Tom Price (56 not out) scored half-centuries to put the hosts in charge.

A brilliant unbeaten 124 from opener Nick Gubbins put Hampshire in total control against Leicestershire . Gubbins hit 15 fours in his 224-ball knock as Hants piled up 255 for three in their second innings, a lead of 225.

Asa Tribe's magnificent 142 not out steered Glamorgan into an even better position against Surrey in their second innings. Tribe's brilliant century led his county to 339 for five in their second innings, a whopping 356 ahead.

In Division Two, Kent look set to keep their promotion hopes alive as closed day two on 84 for two in their chase of 140 against Lancashire .

The hosts took their first-innings total to 214 and a lead of 53 as Zak Crawley made 84 before Matt Milnes, Khaled Ahmed and Keith Dudgeon all took three wickets to help bowl Lancashire out for 192 in their second innings.

They slipped to 22 for two in their chase but Sam Northeast (23) and Tawanda Muyeye (37) put them on the verge of victory.

An unbeaten 87 by Adam Hose and Brett D'Oliveira's 82 helped Worcestershire fight back against Durham . Responding to Durham's 465 all out, the visitors posted 270 for five at the end of day two.

Northamptonshire trail Derbyshire by 62 runs after being bowled out for 310 while Middlesex will aim to build a big lead against Gloucestershire , currently 47 ahead with 10 second-innings wickets intact.

articles.title: County Championship: Leicestershire hit with 27-point deduction and £5000 fine for breaching pitch regulations
articles.summary: Leicestershire have been handed a 27-point deduction and £5000 fine for breaching pitch regulations in August; Watch England's second T20 vs Sri Lanka live on Sky Sports Cricket from 6pm on Thursday (6.30pm first ball)
articles.body:
In a statement on Wednesday, the club said: "The Club notes the Cricket Discipline Panel's decision, which imposes an eight-point deduction, an additional eight-point deduction suspended until the end of the 2027 season, and a financial penalty of £5000.

"Under ECB Rothesay County Championship Playing Condition 16.2.6, the 19 points earned in the match concerned will also be deducted from Leicestershire CCC's 2026 Rothesay County Championship total.

"Accordingly, the Club will lose 27 points overall.

"Having received the Panel's decision, the Club is reviewing its position and considering all available options. No further statement will be issued at this time."

The independent Cricket Discipline Panel (CDP) upheld the Cricket Regulator's charge against Leicestershire for breaching the ECB Pitch Regulations, with the pitch at Uptonsteel Grace Road rated as 'poor' during the County Championship match against Glamorgan, between August 20-23.

If the Foxes fail to beat Hampshire in their ongoing home game, their return to Division Two will be confirmed.

But they face a tough task to do so after Hampshire closed day two on 255-3 in their second innings - a lead of 225.

articles.title: ‘My favorite teammate’: 49ers’ Nick Bosa rekindles bromance after short hiatus
articles.summary: An old 49ers bromance needed only one season apart to pick up where it left off.
articles.body:
An old 49ers bromance needed only one season apart to pick up where it left off.

Nick Bosa and Dre Greenlaw are sharing a defense again after Greenlaw spent 2025 in Denver .

"Dre is my favorite teammate I've ever played with on the field," Bosa said on 95.7 The Game. "To have him back is awesome. He wears his emotions on his sleeve, and you can feel the energy and the anger. When you play defense, it's fun to be a part of."

The 49ers drafted both players in 2019, beginning a six-season partnership defined by speed, physicality and a pair of trips to the Super Bowl.

That run paused when Greenlaw joined the Broncos last year, but his return restored one of the emotional engines of San Francisco's defense .

Greenlaw made his own feelings clear before the opener, calling Bosa "one of your dogs" and saying his presence gave the entire group confidence.

The reunion immediately translated to the field. San Francisco opened the season by dismantling the Rams, 27-7, in Melbourne . Bosa, playing on a managed workload following knee surgery, recorded two tackles for loss and hit Matthew Stafford on the game's first snap.

Greenlaw finished with six tackles and helped hold up Tyler Higbee long enough for Fred Warner to punch the ball loose during a decisive fourth-quarter sequence.

The revitalized 49ers defense limited the reigning MVP to 155 passing yards and did not permit another point after the second quarter.

For Bosa and Greenlaw, the brief separation seemingly reinforced what made their partnership work. Bosa supplies controlled destruction off the edge. Greenlaw delivers the emotion and "anger" behind him.

Their old bromance did not require introductions or an adjustment period.

One game into their reunion, it already looks as if the hiatus never happened.

articles.title: 'He is a God-gifted talent': Rashid Khan on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi - and the skill that is 'hardly' seen at such a young age | EXCLUSIVE
articles.summary: Cricket News: Rashid Khan has been around the India-Afghanistan rivalry long enough to have seen the balance shift. Afghanistan are no longer the side simply hoping.
articles.body: Rashid Khan has been around the India-Afghanistan rivalry long enough to have seen the balance shift. Afghanistan are no longer the side simply hoping to push the bigger teams; there is now a belief within the group that they can beat them.That belief, though, comes with some unfinished work. Ahead of the third and final ODI against India, Rashid sat down with TimesofIndia.com to discuss where Afghanistan still needs to improve, pointing to the powerplay with both bat and ball and the need to develop the mentality to score big.Rashid has also watched India's young players from close quarters. He spent time with Abhishek Sharma at Sunrisers Hyderabad and has witnessed the phenom of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, two players he believes have the skills to go a long way in the game. He explains what makes the pair different and why Sooryavanshi, in particular, has caught his eye at such a young age.For Afghanistan, Rashid sees plenty of talent coming through. Noor Ahmad has already been making an impact, while fast bowler Abdollah Ahmadzai is another name he believes could have a big future.Excerpts:Rashid, results aside, what do you think Afghanistan can take away from this series against India? And when you look at the two teams, where do you see the biggest difference at the moment?I think there are a lot of things we can take from this series. The learning is about how we are going to use the powerplay as a batting unit and what are the areas we need to improve. We see the opposition, how they are scoring runs, and how we are going to manage ourselves to score big runs under any condition, in any situation, and against any bowler. So, it is good learning for the youngsters who have been a part of the team for the first time, and for them, it is a good opportunity to learn from it.But I think if you look at the wickets in Delhi, you always see high-scoring games, and to have that mentality of scoring big is something that is so important. So I think we still have to do a lot of hard work in our batting department. Where we can score those big runs, plus as a bowling unit, we need to find solutions for how we are going to bowl in the powerplay. I think that is so important.If you are giving more than 70-80 runs in the powerplay, it doesn't matter if you are defending 200 or 230. So I think as a team, collectively we have to find the solution for this, and these are the things we take it from here and work on in the future.You have played against many Indian sides, and you have seen different versions of this Indian T20I side as well. What do you make of this Shreyas Iyer-led team now, which has a lot of youngsters coming in?Well, it is a very dangerous side, a destructive side. One after the other, someone is coming who is going to be super destructive, and we all see that they are capable of scoring big. It's not just about scoring; they all have 100s in the T20 format. I think that is something that is dangerous about this team.Players take the game deep, and they score big. It's not like just scoring 20-30 and getting out, I think. And they play fearless cricket. I think in T20, that is how it should be - play fearless. More importantly, they have so much skill, and that is what I think makes them different from any other team.Any young player that you look at and think this is going to be a very important player for this Indian team going forward?I think Abhishek Sharma. I spent so much time with him during SRH; we were very close at that time, and he [always] had that kind of ability and skill. He is doing so well with the bat, but I think he is a very good bowler as well. He has that wonderful skill where he can bowl for you in the middle. So I think he is the one who is going to be a very big package for Team India in the future.Another young sensation who has been doing the rounds is Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. You have bowled to him, and he has made his international debut at the age of 15 as well; but just beyond him being a talented player, what do you think really makes him that special kind of a player?Well, as I mentioned - fearless cricket. And he backs up his skills and knows his shots. I think his shot selection is more important, and he knows his game plan against any side, any bowler, anytime.You hardly see those kinds of things at a very young age; it comes with time, but he already has it. The way he plays fearlessly is what makes him unique. And the power he has, the hand-eye coordination; I think it is something very different. You hardly see that in any [other] player. He is a god-gifted talent.And when you see him, does it remind you of a young Rashid Khan, that fearlessness, that freedom which you used to play?I wasn't that talented, to be honest, at that age, but yes, the skill was there. But I don't know if I could hit those big sixes at that age, how he has been hitting. But as I said, he is a unique talent, and he has shown it not only in the IPL, but even in the Indian team as well, so I think he is someone very special.You have seen Afghanistan cricket go from being underdogs to a team that everybody genuinely thinks can beat the best. When did you actually see that change happening, and what is that next big step for Afghanistan cricket?Well, you know, we have hardly beaten big teams, but when we started, we started here [in India] in the 2023 World Cup, where we beat England; before that, we beat Pakistan in the bilateral T20 series, so I think all of it started from there, and then beating Sri Lanka, beating Pakistan in the World Cup.We did well in Australia & New Zealand at the T20 World Cup [2024], got into the semi-finals, so that belief started that we are in that category where we can beat big teams, so it all started from there. But it's about us now, how we are going to manage and how we keep this continuing.Ibrahim Zadran is now leading the T20I side; you have had a lot of experience leading the side. What do you think makes him an ideal choice, or somebody that you look to and say, this is the guy who can take Afghanistan cricket forward?One thing I like about him is the hard work he puts in, and he is someone who always wants to lead from the front. You need someone like that who is very consistent and who is very straightforward,I think he is the kind of person who is always trying his best to set an example for the youngsters and show them this is the way to go. I think he is a very honest guy, a hard-working guy, and someone who has the ability to lead the team and to help the guys grow with him.And I am always there as a senior player with him to give the support he needs, but he himself is someone who is hard-working and very honest in his job.You mentioned you are there as a senior guy there, but from your experience, what is that one thing that you learned the hard way as a captain that you are telling Ibrahim now?I have learnt so many things. Sometimes you put too much pressure on yourself, which doesn't make it fair. As a captain, you try to put everything on yourself, and that has happened to me.I feel like those are the moments you need to just calm down and focus on your game, focus on your skills, and focus on your game plan. Not think too much about what is going to happen in the result, but think about the process, how it is going to be; as long as you have process in the mind, I think everything will be fine.You are one of the first Afghan cricketers to get that global recognition, and now a generation later there is a young lot of players coming up, if I have to ask you, if you can pick a couple of players that the world should look out for?There is few very good, talented players in Afghanistan coming up. Noor Ahmed has been doing so well, and he is someone who can get to the next level and who can put up some great performances in the future. In the fast-bowling unit as well, I think the area where we need to improve. But there is one fast bowler, Abdollah Ahmadzai, who is in the team now; he is bowling quick. I think if we manage him properly, he is going to be a very quick bowler and a good future for Afghanistan cricket.You have been playing cricket since your teenage years, so there is a lot of injury, workload management, lot of cricket that is happening, so what is Rashid now as compared to young Rashid, how do you manage that workload?One thing is that I used to play a lot of cricket, I used to go one country to another and play all around the world, but it was good for me at that time because I got the experience and I got the knowledge about the condition of different countries. It really helped me at that point, but when I went into surgery and everything, I was struggling. I tried to reduce the cricket as much as possible.I also recently went to the Red Bull Athletic Performance Centre in Austria which gave me a very clear image and idea of my body because I have gone through so many tests and everything and I now know what are the areas I need to improve. I had a very clear picture there with the physio and doctors in moving forward what should I avoid, and where I should play, where I shouldn't play, how much cricket I should play.You started in Afghanistan trying to find ways to play cricket; now you are a global superstar. Looking back and where you are right now, what is it that one thing that is still unfinished for Rashid Khan?Well, one unfinished thing is to win the World Cup for team Afghanistan. That is something which you know I am so much looking forward to. We had a great opportunity in the 2024 [T20] World Cup where we reached the semi-finals, but we couldn't make it to the final. So I think that is something to yearn for - an ICC event [trophy] until I play.I think that is something which I want to have in my book, that yes, an ICC event, be it the T20 World Cup or 50-over World Cup.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
